geometry_source: HCP1065 population bundles, plus an endpoint-filtered estimate from the public Lead-DBS STN pathways; see public-pathways.json.
interpretation: Preset selection is a literature-informed inference. Reference fibers and the explicitly labeled pre-SMA–STN estimate do not represent patient activation, a complete functional circuit or proven causal treatment pathways.
laterality: Bilateral reference bundles are shown by default. The Hemisphere filter controls their visibility. Finding-specific stimulation/effect laterality remains in the cortical highlights and evidence; bilateral fibers do not imply bilateral treatment.

profiles.title: DLPFC · frontostriatal context
profiles.summary: Prefrontal TMS can influence the striatum: TMS–PET demonstrated an ipsilateral caudate dopamine response. The anterior corticostriatal atlas bundle supplies structural context alongside the cortical target.
profiles.limitations: Fox measures DLPFC–sgACC functional connectivity. Seguin proposes one cortical and two fronto-thalamic multistep routes in normative connectomes; neither makes this displayed bundle a direct DLPFC–sgACC tract. These are whole atlas bundles, not fibers selected from a coil site or proven mediators of antidepressant benefit.

bundle_reasons.CS_A: Prefrontal–striatal reference anatomy; TMS–PET supports downstream striatal engagement.

profiles.title: DLPFC · cognitive-control circuitry
profiles.summary: Corticostriatal reference fibers accompany the DLPFC OCD target. Fitzsimmons studied cortical stimulation with ERP; the separate TMS–PET evidence supports a prefrontal influence on the caudate.
profiles.limitations: The displayed tract is anatomical context. The OCD trial did not establish this entire bundle as its treatment mediator, and the healthy-volunteer PET result is not OCD efficacy evidence.

bundle_reasons.CS_A: Associative prefrontal–striatal anatomy; not a reconstruction from the Fitzsimmons trial.

profiles.title: dmPFC · cortico-striatal / thalamic network
profiles.summary: Salomons linked dmPFC treatment response to functional connectivity involving striatum, thalamus and cingulate. Anterior corticostriatal fibers and anterior thalamic radiation show the corresponding broad anatomical systems.
profiles.limitations: Functional MRI does not identify which individual axons carry the effect. Salomons was open label and included bipolar depression; the negative controlled Dunlop 2020 trial remains in the evidence cards.

bundle_reasons.CS_A: Prefrontal–striatal context for the functional network.
bundle_reasons.TR_A: Prefrontal–thalamic context; not a measured TMS activation pathway.

profiles.title: dmPFC · frontostriatal network
profiles.summary: Dunlop associated OCD improvement with reduced dmPFC–ventral-striatal functional connectivity. The striatal and thalamic arms of the wider frontal circuit remain visible as reference anatomy.
profiles.limitations: Dunlop did not reconstruct a treatment-specific tract. The thalamic radiation is broader circuit context, supported by the CSTC rationale in Carmi; it is not a demonstrated Dunlop response fiber. For depression dmPFC findings, see Salomons and the controlled Dunlop 2020 study.

bundle_reasons.CS_A: Frontal–striatal anatomical context for the dmPFC functional finding.
bundle_reasons.TR_A: Thalamic arm of the broader cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuit.

profiles.title: mPFC / ACC · CSTC circuit context
profiles.summary: The H7 OCD approach is motivated by cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuitry. Corticostriatal fibers and anterior thalamic radiation show two available arms of that network.
profiles.limitations: The pallidal links and a complete closed loop are not drawn. Carmi is a clinical trial, not tract-activation mapping; these fibers do not represent the H7 electric field or prove direct stimulation of deep nuclei.

bundle_reasons.CS_A: Frontal–striatal arm of the circuit rationale.
bundle_reasons.TR_A: Frontal–thalamic arm; no synaptic direction or stimulation strength is encoded.

profiles.title: Pre-SMA · striatal and STN circuitry
profiles.summary: Superior corticostriatal fibers show the SMA–striatal arm. A separately colored pre-SMA–STN estimate now shows released STN fibers selected by anatomical endpoints, relevant to the circuitry used by Ji for OCD TMS targeting.
profiles.limitations: The pre-SMA–STN subset uses an approximate anterior-SMA region and a public STN mask in their native template coordinates. It is not Ji’s patient-specific connectivity target. The retained source sets are asymmetric (460 left, 186 right), without artificial mirroring. Superior corticostriatal fibers reach striatum, not STN.

bundle_reasons.CS_S: SMA-complex–striatal reference family, distinct from the STN pathway.
bundle_reasons.HDP_PRE_SMA: Endpoint-filtered STN streamlines; estimated pre-SMA anatomy, not a trial-specific tract.

profiles.title: OFC · frontostriatal / capsular context
profiles.summary: OFC TMS is considered within frontal–striatal circuitry. Jimenez selected a right-OFC site using an OCD DBS tract map through the ALIC; the available capsular tract families supply context.
profiles.limitations: The exact Jimenez ALIC-to-OFC tract is unavailable. Whole anterior corticostriatal and thalamic families do not identify its axons. That report is one case with concurrent ERP. Nauczyciel’s bilateral metabolic effects remain separate from right-sided stimulation.

bundle_reasons.CS_A: Broad OFC/prefrontal–striatal context, not the Jimenez tract.
bundle_reasons.TR_A: ALIC corridor context, not evidence that the whole radiation mediates OFC TMS.

profiles.title: sgACC · indirect network reference
profiles.summary: sgACC is a network reference for DLPFC TMS. Cingulum and corticostriatal anatomy contextualize the wider cingulate–frontal–striatal system; structural anatomy is also described in the SCC DBS literature.
profiles.limitations: Both frontoparietal and parolfactory cingulum segments are available. They do not reconstruct a direct DLPFC–sgACC fiber or the full sequence of Seguin’s indirect connectome routes. SCC DBS anatomy supplies anatomical context, not proof of a TMS mechanism.

bundle_reasons.C_FP: Partial cingulate-network anatomy; this segment is not a complete sgACC connection.
bundle_reasons.CS_A: Frontal–striatal context; not an individually selected sgACC pathway.
bundle_reasons.C_PO: Anterior parolfactory cingulum adds context near the subcallosal region; not a validated sgACC TMS route.

profiles.title: Symptom targets · DLPFC tract context
profiles.summary: The stimulation target remains DLPFC. Its corticostriatal reference fibers stay visible alongside the study’s functional-network targeting layer.
profiles.limitations: The symptom-specific functional map does not identify separate dysphoric and anxiosomatic fiber bundles. The anterior corticostriatal bundle is general DLPFC anatomy, supported by separate mechanistic TMS–PET evidence; it is not a tract result from this targeting trial.

bundle_reasons.CS_A: General DLPFC–striatal context, separate from this study’s functional targeting model.

profiles.title: Insula-guided DLPFC · tract context
profiles.summary: The stimulation target remains DLPFC. Its corticostriatal reference fibers stay visible alongside the study’s functional-network targeting layer.
profiles.limitations: The right-insula–left-DLPFC effective-connectivity relationship is not an anatomical tract. Its cross-hemisphere route is unavailable. The anterior corticostriatal bundle is general DLPFC anatomy, supported by separate mechanistic TMS–PET evidence; it is not a tract result from this targeting trial.

bundle_reasons.CS_A: General DLPFC–striatal context, separate from this study’s functional targeting model.

profiles.title: Depression circuit · DLPFC tract context
profiles.summary: The stimulation target remains DLPFC. Its corticostriatal reference fibers stay visible alongside the study’s functional-network targeting layer.
profiles.limitations: The released functional group map does not identify the tract carrying an individual treatment effect. The anterior corticostriatal bundle is general DLPFC anatomy, supported by separate mechanistic TMS–PET evidence; it is not a tract result from this targeting trial.

bundle_reasons.CS_A: General DLPFC–striatal context, separate from this study’s functional targeting model.

profiles.title: Depression TMS · network overview
profiles.summary: Available striatal, thalamic and cingulate tract families accompany the DLPFC and dmPFC evidence. Choose a target to narrow the suggested fibers.
profiles.limitations: This is a union of reference systems, not one validated antidepressant circuit. The cingulum segment is partial; indirect DLPFC–sgACC routes and individual treatment tractograms are unavailable.

bundle_reasons.C_FP: Partial cingulate anatomy; not a complete subgenual pathway.

profiles.title: OCD TMS · network overview
profiles.summary: Anterior and superior corticostriatal systems and anterior thalamic radiation provide context across medial-frontal, DLPFC, OFC and pre-SMA approaches. Choose a target to narrow the suggested fibers.
profiles.limitations: Reference tract families and an explicitly estimated pre-SMA–STN subset are available. A complete CSTC loop and trial-specific activation maps are not reconstructed.

bundle_reasons.CS_S: SMA-complex–striatal anatomy; not the STN hyperdirect pathway.
bundle_reasons.HDP_PRE_SMA: Anatomical estimate of the pre-SMA–STN connection; separate from corticostriatal fibers.

profiles.title: Fronto-insular mechanism · no inferred tract
profiles.summary: Human regional surfaces orient the evoked-response and connectivity analyses. Animal experiments have no human spatial registration.
profiles.limitations: No default fibers are assigned: functional connectivity, evoked responses and animal interventions do not provide a reconstructed human tract.

profiles.title: Depression therapeutic network · reference anatomy
profiles.summary: Whole structures locate selected network landmarks; the author-released DTN is linked externally and is not displayed.
profiles.limitations: No default fibers are assigned: functional connectivity, evoked responses and animal interventions do not provide a reconstructed human tract.
